newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 1.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0) 171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com -- INDONESIA WARNS OF RISK TO UK ARMS EXPORTS

Indonesia's foreign minister Ali Alatas has warned that if Tony Blair's government continues to press for a link between human rights and equipment sales, the UK could lose its lucrative arms trade with the country. Alatas had met with UK foreign secretary Robin Cook to discuss Britain's review of its defence sales and Cook has made it clear to Alatas that the review was not specifically aimed at Indonesia.
-- TAKEOVER PANEL CHIEF AGREES TO STAY ON

Alistair Defriez has been asked to stay on the Takeover Panel for an extra year to help lead London's efforts to fight off European legislation on the conduct of bids. Defriez believes MEPs should focus more on the safeguarding of jobs than the conduct of takeover bids and justified his stay of an extra year by stressing the importance of 'continuity' and continuing lobbying actions.

Assuming its initial trial is a success, food retailer Safeway is to place Abbey National bank branches in its stores. The installation of a bank would make Safeway the first major food retailer to undertake such a link.
Professor Douglas McWilliams, founder of the Centre for Economic and Business research, has expressed fears that the windfall taxes on businesses are 'damaging' and 'will cost jobs'.
-- DATE SET FOR NEXT WAVE OF GAS COMPETITION

Gas market regulator Ofgas announced on Monday that the next wave of competition in the market would begin in November. From November 1, as many as 2.6 million customers in Scotland and northern Britain will be able to buy gas from any supplier. Competition will then be spread across the country in five stages, with full competition throughout the country to be finalised in June 1998.
-- PLAN TO BUY POWER PLANTS TO BURN BSE WASTE
The government is considering hiring unused power stations to burn hundreds of thousands of tonnes of waste left from cattle slaughtered due to the BSE scare.
Anderson Consulting, the world's largest accounting and consulting organisation, has appointed Robert Grafton as temporary chief executive while it tries to mend internal divisions.

Japanese electronics group NEC has invested a further $285 million into Packard Bell-NEC, raising its in total investment in the US computer company to more than $1 billion. The money is to be used to support Packard Bell NEC's establishment of direct sales operations aimed at corporate customers.
